issues.title: Cut non-inlined VARCHAR group-key overhead in the radix aggregate (measure per phase, fix the largest delta)
issues.hypothesis: In the q16 count(DISTINCT) aggregate, a non-inlined VARCHAR group key (p_type, 25 chars, which CompressedMaterialization cannot pack because it is longer than 16 bytes) roughly doubles the aggregate's cost. Planner A/B on a temp table of the q16 join output (1.18M rows), 8 threads, warm: `SELECT hb, h, p_size, count(DISTINCT ps_suppkey) ... GROUP BY ALL` with h = hash(p_type) BIGINT gives HASH_GROUP_BY 0.10 s CPU and 45-48 ms wall. The same query with p_type VARCHAR gives 0.22 s CPU and 82-87 ms wall. The scan is 0.01 s in both, so the difference is inside the aggregate. Weaker evidence: SELECT DISTINCT on the 4 keys is 46-59 ms with p_type vs 35-37 ms with h, and a plain GROUP BY count(*) over 28k groups is 34-46 ms vs 20 ms. In q16 the aggregate is about 90 of the ~155 ms wall (the join-only query is 62 ms warm), so removing most of this ~100 ns/row string penalty is worth ~25-40 ms. Rows carrying a non-inlined string go through several stages: distinct-HT AppendUnified, which computes heap sizes and scatters into the heap; abandon/repartition, which copies the heap and recomputes pointers (TupleDataAllocator::RecomputeHeapPointers); the distinct finalize GroupedAggregateHashTable::Combine, which gathers via FlushMoveState and re-scatters new groups with another heap copy; then a re-hash and re-sink into the main HT, and the main finalize Combine. Earlier sink-side tweaks (E0001-E0003) never isolated the string cost.
issues.plan: Step 1, measure (cheap). Add temporary timers following the E0002 pattern: Printer::RawPrint from gstate destructors. Time these phases: RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink (FindOrCreateGroups / AppendUnified), MaybeRepartition, RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize -> GroupedAggregateHashTable::Combine (src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp:883), the re-sink in HashAggregateDistinctFinalizeTask::AggregateDistinctGrouping (physical_hash_aggregate.cpp:648-754), and the main finalize. Run the temp-table A/B twice: `CREATE TEMP TABLE t AS SELECT p_brand, p_type, p_size, ps_suppkey, hash(p_type) h, hash(p_brand) hb FROM <q16 join>`, then compare GROUP BY hb,h,p_size against hb,p_type,p_size with count(DISTINCT ps_suppkey). Find the phase with the largest VARCHAR-vs-BIGINT delta. Inside it, look at per-chunk heap work in src/common/types/row/ (tuple_data_collection.cpp, tuple_data_allocator.cpp, tuple_data_scatter_gather.cpp): ComputeHeapSizes, Build, RecomputeHeapPointers or FindHeapPointers on scan or pin, and chunk-part splitting when 300-row input chunks each open new heap parts. Step 2: fix that one mechanism. Candidate fixes, depending on the evidence: (a) skip RecomputeHeapPointers or the heap-pointer search when the heap blocks have not moved (in-memory, still pinned); (b) in Combine and Repartition of heap layouts, copy row and heap data in bulk per chunk part instead of per row; (c) avoid creating many small heap chunk parts for small input chunks. Keep the diff to one mechanism.
issues.expected_gain: q16 10-25%. The aggregate is ~90 of ~155 ms, and the string penalty measured on the same data is ~40 ms wall.
issues.generality: Any hash aggregate, DISTINCT, or count(DISTINCT) grouped by strings longer than 12 bytes (names, types, comments, URLs). These are very common in analytical workloads. Joins and sorts also benefit if the fix lands in shared TupleData code. Risk of slowdown: little, if the change only removes redundant work. Spilling (external) aggregates must keep the pointer recomputation that unpin/repin needs.
issues.risk: Medium. TupleData heap-pointer invariants are subtle; skipping a recompute when blocks did move corrupts strings. Must test the external/spill path (e.g. SET memory_limit low with a large VARCHAR GROUP BY), plus lists/structs in group keys. Correctness is checked on hidden shapes.
